  there's a second demo-able story by H8.
- **Role B**: wire the Anthropic SDK, get `summarizeDecisionTrail()`
  producing real output against the seeded battery audit log. This is the
  highest-leverage function in the app — prioritize it over everything
  else in your doc.
- **Role C**: real car visual for the landing page (static image + hotspot
  overlay, minimum; 360 viewer if time allows). This is the first thing
  judges see — don't let it stay a wireframe SVG past H4.
- **Role D**: standalone audit trail view with filtering (US-8.1, 8.4).

**Checkpoint H4**: everyone demos their piece to the group, 2 min each.
Merge anything stable into `main`.

## H4 - H8 — Integration + depth
- **Role A**: wire real `ingest`/`enrich` stage transitions to the pipeline
  strip so Role C's UI shows real progress, not just seeded "complete"
  states. Start on multi-market support if ingestion is solid.
- **Role B**: `reassessChallenge()` and `summarizeStakeholderReviews()` real
  implementations. Test the full "PM challenges → AI re-assesses → states
  whether it changed" loop live against the UI.
- **Role C**: pipeline strip polish, live-refresh on stage changes, start
  the sensitivity view (US-4.4) if the weight-slider mechanic needs it to
  feel complete.
- **Role D**: audit log CSV export, low-confidence queue (US-7.2).

**Checkpoint H8 (roughly halfway)**: full run-through as a group, PM
persona end to end: land → open/create a workflow → review requirements →
challenge one → see stakeholder reviews come in → approve. Fix anything
that breaks this path before adding more features — this path *is* the
demo.

## H8 - H12 — Breadth + second component
- Get a second component (beyond battery) demo-ready end to end, ideally
  one where the PM *rejects* a requirement (shows the full decision
  spectrum, not just approve). Role A seeds/ingests it, Role B's AI
  functions run against it for real, Roles C/D confirm the UI holds up
  with different data shapes (e.g. a requirement with zero stakeholder
  reviews yet, or all-reject).
- Epic 2 signal extraction (`extractSignals`, Role B) from real verbatims,
  if ingestion (Role A) is ready.
- Stretch items from each role's doc, time permitting, in the priority
  order listed there — don't start a role's "stretch" section if their
  "must have" isn't demo-stable yet.

## H12 - H14 — Feature freeze, bug bash
- **No new features after H12** unless something is badly broken. Switch
  entirely to: click through every view on a clean `npm install && npm run
  dev`, fix what's broken, tighten copy, fix loading/empty states.
- Confirm `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx next lint` are both clean.
- Confirm the demo narrative survives a hard refresh at every step (no
  state that only exists because of a specific click order).

## H14 - H16 — Demo prep
- Write the 3-minute demo script: landing page (show the concept) → open
  battery workflow (show pipeline + AI summary) → challenge a requirement
  live (show the AI re-assessment loop — this is your best "wow" moment) →
  switch to stakeholder view, submit a review (show it land back in the PM
  view's audit trail) → show the audit log / traceability view (prove the
  "transparent decision-support" claim from the brief).
- Record a fallback screen capture of the full demo in case live demo
  breaks — `npm run build && npm run start` once to confirm production
  build works, not just dev mode.
- Prepare the pitch framing around the evaluation criteria table in
  `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` — name-check "decision and scoring logic",
  "traceability and auditability", etc. explicitly, since that's literally
  how this gets scored.

## H16 - H17 — Buffer
Things go wrong. This hour exists so that when they do, you're not cutting
into demo prep.

Everything's in place and untracked, ready for an initial commit whenever you want one — I'll leave that to you per your own commit conventions. Here's where things stand:

## What's built (v0, verified working end-to-end)

A working Next.js 14 + TypeScript + Tailwind app at `/Users/navneetkishansrinivasan/Desktop/ehl-alpha`, with all three views wired to a real (in-memory) backend and tested live in the browser:

- **Landing page** — BMW 5 Series with clickable component hotspots, blue = has workflow, gray = create new
- **PM workflow page** — GitHub-Actions-style pipeline strip, AI decision-trail summary, requirement cards with explainable scores + live weight sliders, approve/reject/postpone/**challenge** actions, PR-reviewer-style stakeholder panel with AI overview, evidence/sources drill-down, limitations panel, live audit trail sidebar
- **Stakeholder review page** — summary, per-factor score charts, free-text expert opinion, approve/not-approve

The whole audit-log → AI-summary mechanism you described (PM disagrees → log captures it → summary narrates the before/after) is implemented and seeded with a believable story on the Battery & Charging component, so the app demos convincingly with zero setup (`npm install && npm run dev`).

Type-checks clean, lints clean, production build succeeds.

## Docs for your team

- [README.md](README.md) — setup + architecture
- [docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md](docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md) — challenge recap, our concept, user-story prioritization, evaluation-criteria mapping
- [docs/ROLE_A_BACKEND.md](docs/ROLE_A_BACKEND.md), [ROLE_B_AI.md](docs/ROLE_B_AI.md), [ROLE_C_PM_FRONTEND.md](docs/ROLE_C_PM_FRONTEND.md), [ROLE_D_STAKEHOLDER_TRUST.md](docs/ROLE_D_STAKEHOLDER_TRUST.md) — each dev's task list, file ownership, and exact swap-out points for Claude Code/Codex agents to pick up
- [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md) — hour-by-hour plan for a 15-17h build, with a clear "must have" path and checkpoints at H4/H8/H12

One thing worth knowing: Next.js is pinned to 14.2.35 (not latest) because your machine runs Node 18 — latest Next requires Node 20+. If your teammates are all on Node 20+, that's an easy one-line bump in `package.json`, but I'd keep everyone on the same version to avoid "works on my machine" during the hackathon.

content: how did you score the reviews, if its hard-coded, how would you recommend to go about?

message.content: how did you score the reviews, if its hard-coded, how would you recommend to go about?

content.text:
Yes — right now it's entirely hardcoded. Two separate things are faked, and they need different fixes:

## What's hardcoded today

**1. Score factor raw values** — in [seed.ts](src/lib/seed.ts), each requirement's `scoreFactors` (customer_impact: 88, frequency: 82, sales_relevance: 75...) are hand-picked numbers I wrote to tell a believable story. The *weighting math* is real (`recomputeScore()` in [db.ts](src/lib/db.ts:168) does an actual weighted sum, and the sliders in `RequirementCard` genuinely recompute live) — but the inputs it's averaging are fiction.

**2. Stakeholder review decisions** — also hand-written in seed.ts (Engineering approves, Legal rejects with a specific rationale, etc.). This is fixture history to make the demo look lived-in, not something the app computed.

## How I'd recommend making each one real

These seven factors split cleanly into three categories — don't treat them uniformly:

**Deterministic, no AI needed — compute directly from real data:**
- `frequency` — literally `Signal.frequency`, the count from clustering real verbatims. Already a real number once Role A's ingestion + Role B's `extractSignals()` run for real.
- `sales_relevance` — a formula over the sales dataset (BEV mix growth × volume in target market), not a judgment call.
- `evidence_strength` — should be a formula over source count × reliability tier (strong = 3+ sources incl. first-party, moderate = 2, weak = 1/web-only — this is already spelled out in [ROLE_B_AI.md](docs/ROLE_B_AI.md)), not something you ask an LLM to self-rate. An LLM guessing its own confidence is exactly the kind of ungrounded number the brief warns against.

**LLM-assisted, but constrained and cited — never a bare number:**
- `customer_impact`, `competitive_gap`, `strategic_fit` — these require reading unstructured evidence (verbatims, competitor web sources, the BMW annual report) and judging magnitude. Use structured output so the model returns `{ value: 0-100, citedSourceIds: [...], rationale: "..." }`, and log the source ids + rationale to the audit trail alongside the score. That's what makes it defensible in front of judges — "why is this 90?" should always answer with specific evidence, never "the model said so."

**Should come from a human, not AI:**
- `effort` (inverse) — an AI estimating engineering effort is pure speculation. Better: AI proposes a placeholder, flagged `unvalidated`, and it only becomes a real input once an Engineering stakeholder's review confirms or overrides it through the review form you already have built. This also gives Engineering's review actual teeth in the score, not just a comment thread.

**Stakeholder decisions specifically**: don't try to predict or auto-generate these at all — they're real human input through the stakeholder page that's already built (`PATCH /api/reviews/:id`). The only thing AI should touch there is *summarizing* the reviews that come in (`summarizeStakeholderReviews()`), never generating the decisions themselves.

## The one guardrail I'd hold firm on

Keep `rawValue` (data/AI-derived) and `weight` (PM's priority call) separate, like the schema already does — don't let a PM directly edit a `rawValue`. If a PM disagrees with a score input, that's exactly what the **challenge flow** (US-6.3, already wired in `RequirementCard` → `POST /api/requirements/:id/challenge`) is for: it forces the disagreement through a logged re-assessment instead of a silent overwrite, which is the difference between "transparent decision support" and just a spreadsheet with extra steps.

input.content:
# Real data setup

The app is grounded in the real BMW hackathon datasets: 13,771 real customer
feedback rows across three vehicle lines, real sales volumes, real
multi-market customer-study benchmarks, and the real official equipment/
pricing documents. **None of this is in git** — it's confidential hackathon
material, not something to publish on a public repo. Every teammate needs
their own local copy.

## One-time setup (everyone, ~2 minutes)

1. Get the dataset files from wherever the team shared them (`F70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`, `G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`, `G70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`, `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx`, `sales_volumes.xlsx`, `F70_OptionList.PDF`, `G60_OptionList.PDF`, `G70_OptionList.PDF`).
2. Copy all 8 files into `data-raw/` at the repo root (gitignored — create the folder if it doesn't exist).
3. Convert the 3 PDFs to text (needs `poppler`: `brew install poppler` on macOS):
   ```bash
   cd data-raw
   for f in F70_OptionList G60_OptionList G70_OptionList; do
     pdftotext -layout "$f.PDF" "$f.txt"
   done
   cd ..
   ```
4. Run the ingestion pipeline:
   ```bash
   npm run ingest
   ```
   This writes `src/data/*.json` (also gitignored). Restart `npm run dev` to pick it up.

Without this, the app still runs — `src/lib/seed.ts` falls back to a small
hand-written mock workflow so nobody is blocked waiting on file access. You'll
know you're on the fallback if the landing page shows only one vehicle
("BMW 5 Series") with one workflow instead of three vehicles with ~17
workflows.

## What's actually in the data

| File | Rows/sheets | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{F70,G60,G70}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` | ~4,000-5,000 rows each, sheet `Feedback_Explorer` | Real customer verbatims with BMW's own **VFC (Vehicle Feedback Classification)** taxonomy already applied: `Feedback Type` (Likes/Wants/Difficult to Use/Defect), `Vfc level2 Name` / `Vfc level3 Name` (226 real categories), country, engine type (ICE/BEVE/PHEV). |
| `sales_volumes.xlsx` | 3 sheets (`F70`, `G60_G68`, `G70`), 4 rows each | 2024/2025/2030(est.) sales volume by market. |
| `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx` | `CN_EU_2025` (36 categories × 5 models, direct 0-10 means), `US_2025` (satisfaction-bucket distributions for G60/G70) | Customer-study ratings comparing BMW models to each other — **not** external competitors. |
| `{F70,G60,G70}_OptionList.PDF` | Official BMW price/equipment configurator documents (German) | Standard/optional equipment by trim. |

F70 = 1 Series, G60 = 5 Series (G68 is its China long-wheelbase variant),
G70 = 7 Series.

## How ingestion turns this into the app's data model

See `scripts/ingest-real-data.ts` (the pipeline) and `scripts/lib/componentMap.ts`
(the category mapping) for the actual code. The short version:

1. **Feedback → FeedbackRecord[]**: straight column mapping, written to `src/data/feedback.json`. This is what powers the Evidence Explorer (`/evidence`).
2. **Component mapping**: BMW's 226 `Vfc level2 Name` categories are mapped onto our 6 landing-page components (exterior/interior/windows/steering/engine/battery) by keyword rules in `componentMap.ts` — deterministic and auditable on purpose, not an LLM call. Unmatched categories go to a `general` bucket (still browsable in the Evidence Explorer, just no landing-page hotspot).
3. **Signals**: feedback grouped by `(vehicleCode, component, theme)`, with real frequency counts and a `Feedback Type` breakdown standing in for sentiment — written to `src/data/signals.json`.
4. **Requirements**: `src/lib/deriveRequirements.ts` picks up to 4 signals per component (prioritizing pain points, then customer-requested gaps, then strengths worth protecting) and scores them **deterministically** — no LLM involved in v0's scoring. See that file's top comment for exactly which factors are real data vs. which are placeholders (`effort_inverse` is always a flat placeholder; `competitive_gap`/`strategic_fit` are the two factors Role B should eventually upgrade to a real LLM call with cited evidence — see `docs/ROLE_B_AI.md`).
5. **Sales relevance / competitive gap**: computed from real `sales_volumes.xlsx` growth and real `customer-study` cross-model comparisons — see the `STUDY_CATEGORY_KEYWORDS` mapping in `deriveRequirements.ts` for how customer-study categories (a *different* taxonomy than VFC) are matched to our 6 components.
6. **Equipment PDFs**: chunked by section header into raw text excerpts (`src/data/equipment-chunks.json`) for citation. **Known gap**: this does not parse the standard/optional equipment matrix into a structured per-trim feature table — the PDF's column-aligned layout (10+ trim columns, "■" markers) is brittle to parse reliably from `pdftotext -layout` output in the time available. If someone wants to extend this: the raw text is at `data-raw/*_OptionList.txt` after the pdftotext step, and the "AUSGEWÄHLTE SERIENAUSSTATTUNGEN" sections contain the matrix.

## The one hand-authored piece

Everything above is data-driven. The one exception: the BMW 5 Series /
Battery & Charging workflow (`wf_g60_battery`) has a scripted PM-challenge
→ AI-revision → stakeholder-review narrative layered on top of its
real top requirement, so the demo has a complete decision-trail story to
walk through even before Role B wires in live OpenAI calls. The requirement
title/numbers it references are computed live from real data (re-running
`npm run ingest` will shift them if the source data changes); only the
stakeholder dialogue and PM's challenge text are scripted. See
`buildFlagshipNarrative()` in `src/lib/seed.ts`.

## If you need to re-derive the mapping decisions

`scripts/lib/componentMap.ts`'s keyword rules were built by inspecting the
full 226-category list once (`node -e` one-liner over the parsed xlsx — not
checked in, but trivial to re-run with `XLSX.readFile` + a `Counter`-style
tally). If a re-ingest surfaces a miscategorized theme, the fix is a keyword
rule or an `OVERRIDES` entry in that file, not a code path change.

| `{F70,G60,G70}_OptionList.PDF` | Official BMW price/equipment configurator documents (German) | Standard/optional equipment by trim. |

F70 = 1 Series, G60 = 5 Series (G68 is its China long-wheelbase variant),
G70 = 7 Series.

## How ingestion turns this into the app's data model

See `scripts/ingest-real-data.ts` (the pipeline) and `scripts/lib/componentMap.ts`
(the category mapping) for the actual code. The short version:

1. **Feedback → FeedbackRecord[]**: straight column mapping, written to `src/data/feedback.json`. This is what powers the Evidence Explorer (`/evidence`).
2. **Component mapping**: BMW's 226 `Vfc level2 Name` categories are mapped onto our 6 landing-page components (exterior/interior/windows/steering/engine/battery) by keyword rules in `componentMap.ts` — deterministic and auditable on purpose, not an LLM call. Unmatched categories go to a `general` bucket (still browsable in the Evidence Explorer, just no landing-page hotspot).
3. **Signals**: feedback grouped by `(vehicleCode, component, theme)`, with real frequency counts and a `Feedback Type` breakdown standing in for sentiment — written to `src/data/signals.json`.
4. **Requirements**: `src/lib/deriveRequirements.ts` picks up to 4 signals per component (prioritizing pain points, then customer-requested gaps, then strengths worth protecting) and scores them **deterministically** — no LLM involved in v0's scoring. See that file's top comment for exactly which factors are real data vs. which are placeholders (`effort_inverse` is always a flat placeholder; `competitive_gap`/`strategic_fit` are the two factors Role B should eventually upgrade to a real LLM call with cited evidence — see `docs/ROLE_B_AI.md`).
5. **Sales relevance / competitive gap**: computed from real `sales_volumes.xlsx` growth and real `customer-study` cross-model comparisons — see the `STUDY_CATEGORY_KEYWORDS` mapping in `deriveRequirements.ts` for how customer-study categories (a *different* taxonomy than VFC) are matched to our 6 components.
6. **Equipment PDFs**: chunked by section header into raw text excerpts (`src/data/equipment-chunks.json`) for citation. **Known gap**: this does not parse the standard/optional equipment matrix into a structured per-trim feature table — the PDF's column-aligned layout (10+ trim columns, "■" markers) is brittle to parse reliably from `pdftotext -layout` output in the time available. If someone wants to extend this: the raw text is at `data-raw/*_OptionList.txt` after the pdftotext step, and the "AUSGEWÄHLTE SERIENAUSSTATTUNGEN" sections contain the matrix.

## The one hand-authored piece

Everything above is data-driven. The one exception: the BMW 5 Series /
Battery & Charging workflow (`wf_g60_battery`) has a scripted PM-challenge
→ AI-revision → stakeholder-review narrative layered on top of its
real top requirement, so the demo has a complete decision-trail story to
walk through even before Role B wires in live OpenAI calls. The requirement
title/numbers it references are computed live from real data (re-running
`npm run ingest` will shift them if the source data changes); only the
stakeholder dialogue and PM's challenge text are scripted. See
`buildFlagshipNarrative()` in `src/lib/seed.ts`.

## If you need to re-derive the mapping decisions

`scripts/lib/componentMap.ts`'s keyword rules were built by inspecting the
full 226-category list once (`node -e` one-liner over the parsed xlsx — not
checked in, but trivial to re-run with `XLSX.readFile` + a `Counter`-style
tally). If a re-ingest surfaces a miscategorized theme, the fix is a keyword
rule or an `OVERRIDES` entry in that file, not a code path change.

# BMW Requirements Copilot

AI-assisted product requirement derivation, prioritization and human-in-the-loop
review for BMW's "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon challenge.

Read [`docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md`](docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md) first — it has the challenge,
our concept, and how user stories map to what's built. Then
[`docs/DATA_SETUP.md`](docs/DATA_SETUP.md) to get the real datasets running
locally. Then read your role doc in `docs/`.

## Stack

- Next.js 14 (App Router, pinned for Node 18 compatibility — don't bump to 15/16
  mid-hackathon unless everyone upgrades Node to 20+)
- TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 3
- In-memory data store (`src/lib/db.ts`), seeded from **real BMW hackathon
  data** (13,771 verbatims, sales volumes, customer-study benchmarks) via
  `npm run ingest` — see [`docs/DATA_SETUP.md`](docs/DATA_SETUP.md). Falls
  back to a small hand-written mock if the real data isn't present locally,
  so nobody is blocked.
- AI layer (`src/lib/ai.ts`) targets **OpenAI** (the team's budget). Every
  function is currently a deterministic mock so the app works end-to-end
  with no API key; requirement scoring itself is already real/deterministic
  from the ingested data (see `src/lib/deriveRequirements.ts`) — the mocked
  functions are the narrative/summary layer on top. See
  [`docs/ROLE_B_AI.md`](docs/ROLE_B_AI.md).

## Setup

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Requires Node >=18.17 (Node 20+ also fine).

For the real data (strongly recommended — see
[`docs/DATA_SETUP.md`](docs/DATA_SETUP.md)):

```bash
# copy the 8 dataset files into data-raw/, convert the 3 PDFs with pdftotext, then:
npm run ingest
```

## Project structure

```
src/
  lib/
    types.ts            # shared domain types — the team contract, read this first
    db.ts                # in-memory store + all read/write functions (Role A owns)
    seed.ts              # assembles real workflows from src/data/*.json, or falls back to a mock
    realData.ts          # loader for the ingested JSON fixtures
    deriveRequirements.ts # deterministic requirement derivation + scoring from real data
    ai.ts                # mocked AI functions (Role B replaces internals, targets OpenAI)
    api-client.ts        # typed fetch wrappers — frontend only talks to the API through here
  app/
    page.tsx                                # landing page (car hotspots, vehicle switcher)
    workflow/[componentId]/page.tsx         # PM workflow view (Role C)
    stakeholder/[workflowId]/[stakeholderId]/page.tsx  # stakeholder review (Role D)
    evidence/page.tsx                       # Evidence Explorer — filterable table over all real feedback (Role D)
    api/...                                 # REST routes, thin wrappers around lib/db.ts
  components/
    charts/              # MetricBar, GroupedBarChart — real SVG charts, no charting library
    ...                  # EvidenceBadge, PipelineStrip, AuditLogPanel, RequirementCard, ReviewerRow, CarHotspotViewer
scripts/
  ingest-real-data.ts    # offline pipeline: data-raw/*.xlsx,*.PDF -> src/data/*.json
  lib/componentMap.ts    # maps BMW's 226 real VFC feedback categories onto our 6 components
data-raw/                # gitignored — the real BMW datasets, copy your own in
src/data/                # gitignored — ingest script output, regenerate with `npm run ingest`
```

## Demo data

With real data ingested: 3 vehicle lines (BMW 1/5/7 Series), ~17 of 18
possible component workflows populated from real signals, a dedicated
Evidence Explorer over all 13,771 real feedback rows, and one fully
narrated flagship workflow (BMW 5 Series · Battery & Charging) showing
the PM-challenge → AI-revision → stakeholder-review loop end to end,
grounded in real numbers. See [`docs/DATA_SETUP.md`](docs/DATA_SETUP.md)
for exactly how each dataset becomes app data.

Without real data (fallback): one hand-written "battery" workflow for the
BMW 5 Series, enough to demo the mechanics with placeholder numbers.

## Known tradeoffs (intentional, for a 15-17h build)

- In-memory store, not a real DB. Swap-out point is clearly marked in `db.ts`.
- AI narrative layer (`ai.ts`) is mocked with templated text, not live OpenAI
  calls, by default — scoring itself is already real/deterministic. Swap-out
  points are documented in `ai.ts` and `docs/ROLE_B_AI.md`.
- Equipment PDF parsing stops at section-level text chunks, not a structured
  per-trim feature matrix — see the "known gap" note in `docs/DATA_SETUP.md`.
- `competitive_gap`/`sales_relevance`/`strategic_fit` score factors are
  computed per-component, not per-requirement-theme (customer-study and
  sales data isn't granular enough for the latter) — so requirements for the
  same component share those three factor values. Documented in each
  factor's `rationale` field, visible in the UI.
- Next.js pinned to 14.2.35 (not latest) for Node 18 compatibility across the
  team. `npm audit` will show Next.js platform CVEs fixed only in 15+ — not a
  concern for a localhost demo, but don't deploy this build publicly without
  upgrading first. Same applies to the `xlsx` package (dev-only, used by the
  ingestion script against trusted local files).
- **The real BMW datasets, and anything derived from them, must never be
  committed** — `data-raw/` and `src/data/*.json` are gitignored. Code that
  reads them is fine to commit; the data itself is not.

    db.ts            # in-memory store + all read/write functions (Role A owns)
    seed.ts          # demo data: one fully-populated "battery" workflow
    ai.ts            # mocked AI functions (Role B replaces internals)
    api-client.ts    # typed fetch wrappers — frontend only talks to the API through here
  app/
    page.tsx                                # landing page (car hotspots)
    workflow/[componentId]/page.tsx         # PM workflow view (Role C)
    stakeholder/[workflowId]/[stakeholderId]/page.tsx  # stakeholder review (Role D)
    api/...                                 # REST routes, thin wrappers around lib/db.ts
  components/        # shared UI: EvidenceBadge, PipelineStrip, AuditLogPanel, RequirementCard, ReviewerRow, CarHotspotViewer
```

## Demo data

The seed pre-populates a **Battery & Charging** workflow for the BMW 5 Series
(Europe market) with 3 requirements, 4 stakeholders, partially-submitted
reviews, and ~17 audit log entries telling a believable story: AI derives a
vague first draft → PM challenges it → AI revises with a concrete target →
stakeholders review → PM is mid-decision. This is what you see immediately on
`npm run dev`, no setup needed. The other 5 components (exterior, interior,
windows, steering, engine) have no workflow yet, to demo the "create new"
flow from the landing page.

## Known tradeoffs (intentional, for a 15-17h build)

- In-memory store, not a real DB. Swap-out point is clearly marked in `db.ts`.
- AI layer is mocked with templated text, not live Claude calls. Swap-out
  point is clearly marked in `ai.ts`, with the exact input/output shape Role
  B needs to preserve.

  team. `npm audit` will show Next.js platform CVEs fixed only in 15+ — not a
  concern for a localhost demo, but don't deploy this build publicly without
  upgrading first.

  all 6 components — depth over breadth for the judged demo.

# Project brief

## The challenge (BMW Group)

> What should the next generation of a BMW vehicle offer its customers? Build
> an AI-powered application that helps product managers derive, justify, and
> prioritize customer requirements for a successor vehicle. Ground your
> proposals in customer feedback, BMW product and sales data, and relevant web
> research — while keeping the product manager firmly in control of every
> decision.

Scope: BMW 1/5/7 Series (or a combination), Europe/China/US (or a subset),
3-5 years out. For each vehicle we get customer feedback (verbatims),
equipment data, sales volumes, and a customer study; we may enrich with
external sources (competitor info, reviews, market/tech trends).

**What judges want to see** (from the brief, verbatim):
1. A concept + working prototype showing AI supporting identification,
   formulation and prioritization of customer-facing requirements.
2. A representative set of requirements with clear evidence and reasoning.
3. A transparent decision-support experience: PM can review, challenge,
   modify, approve, or reject AI proposals, with evidence/assumptions/
   uncertainties/decisions visible and traceable throughout.

**Explicitly out of scope**: engineering specs, regulatory requirements,
detailed business-case calculations. Focus on customer value.

**Internal framing** (from BMW's own PM keynote, for flavor/credibility in
the demo narrative): the real process goes from ~1 billion findings → ~1,000
requirements → one car. A "requirement" = a customer-relevant attribute of
the car. The real pipeline is: situation analysis → AI structures/clusters/
contextualizes findings → requirements definition (baseline: previous BMW
model, portfolio, sales volume, competition, customer/public feedback,
trends) → specification & quantification (measurable targets, e.g. "range:
600 or 700 mi?") → prioritization → documentation → requirements tracking.
Our workflow pipeline stages mirror this shape.

## Our concept

Three views:

1. **Landing page** — a BMW 5 Series with hotspot dots on components
   (exterior, interior, windows, steering, powertrain, battery). Click a dot:
   open its requirements workflow if one exists, or start a new one.
2. **PM workflow page** (per component) — a GitHub-Actions-style pipeline
   strip (ingest → enrich → extract → derive → score → stakeholder review →
   PM decision → deploy), an AI-generated decision-trail summary, the
   requirement list with explainable scores and adjustable weights, a
   PR-reviewer-style stakeholder panel with an AI overview of where
   reviewers agree/disagree, and a live audit trail sidebar.
3. **Stakeholder review page** — summary of the requirement + evidence
   (charts from real score factors), the AI's running decision-trail
   summary, a free-text expert-opinion field, and approve/not-approve.

**The mechanism that ties it together**: every stage transition, every AI
proposal, every PM decision (approve/reject/postpone/**challenge**), and
every stakeholder review is written to an **append-only audit log**
(`src/lib/types.ts` → `AuditLogEntry`). The AI summaries shown on both the PM
and stakeholder pages are (in the real version) generated *from* that log —
when a PM disagrees and asks for changes, the next AI summary should
narrate what was asked, what was proposed, what the PM pushed back on, and
how the proposal changed. The v0 seed data (`src/lib/seed.ts`) hand-writes
one such story for the battery/charging requirement so the mechanism is
demoable without live AI calls; Role B's job is to make it real.

## User stories → what we're building (prioritized for 15-17h)

We will not build all 9 epics to full depth. Priority order for the time box:

**Must have for the demo (Epics 6, 8, 9, slice of 3/4):**
- US-6.1, 6.2, 6.4 — PM can approve/reject/postpone/challenge with required
  rationale on reject/postpone; evidence shown next to every decision.
  (Built in v0: `RequirementCard`, `PATCH /api/requirements/:id`.)
- US-6.3 — PM challenges a score/rationale, AI re-assesses and states
  whether it changed. (Built in v0 as a mock: `POST /api/requirements/:id/challenge`.)
- US-8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.5 — full trace, append-only, actor+timestamp+old/new
  value+rationale on every entry, AI vs human distinguished.
  (Built in v0: `AuditLogEntry`, `logAction()`, `AuditLogPanel`.)
- US-9.1 — defined workflow with stage ownership (ai/pm/stakeholder) shown.
  (Built in v0: `Stage`, `PipelineStrip`.)
- US-3.1, 3.3 — requirements have id, description, linked findings/sources,
  evidence level, assumptions, uncertainties, category, status "Proposed".
  (Built in v0, seeded.)
- US-4.1, 4.2, 4.3 — explainable weighted score, live-adjustable weights,
  evidence level shown next to score. (Built in v0: `scoreFactors`,
  weight sliders in `RequirementCard`.)
- US-7.1, 7.2, 7.3 — missing/thin/contradictory evidence surfaced; weak
  evidence flagged; limitations panel. (Built in v0: `EvidenceBadge`,
  `AISummary` type "limitations".)

**Should have, reach during the build (Epics 1, 2, 5):**
- US-1.1 — real dataset upload/ingestion (v0 only has seeded sources).
- US-2.1 through 2.7 — real signal clustering from uploaded verbatims
  (v0 has a mock `extractSignals()` in `ai.ts`).
- US-5.1 — vehicle/derivative/market selector (v0 only has market at
  workflow-creation time).

**Could have, only if time remains (Epic 1.4, 5.4, 9.2, 9.4, 9.5):**
- Config-driven new data sources, onboarding another model/market without
  code changes, re-running the pipeline on new data with a diff view,
  exporting approved requirements to CSV/Jira.

## Evaluation criteria mapping (from the brief's organizers)

| Criterion | Primary epics | Where in this repo |
|---|---|---|
| Decision and scoring logic | Epic 4, US-7.1 | `scoreFactors`, `EvidenceBadge`, weight sliders |
| Workflow and human decision-making | Epic 6, US-9.1 | `PipelineStrip`, `RequirementCard` actions |
| Traceability and auditability | Epic 8, US-2.6 | `AuditLogPanel`, `logAction()` |
| Solution quality, usability, feasibility | Epics 3, 5, US-4.2 | requirement cards, live weight sliders |
| Innovation, scalability, business impact | US-1.4, 5.4, 9.2 | talk track for the pitch — be honest that this is a v0, point at the swap-out points as the scalability story |

## Non-goals for this hackathon

Do not spend time on: engineering specs, regulatory/homologation detail,
business-case ROI math, auth/accounts, a real database, production
deployment hardening. If in doubt, cut it — a working, honest, traceable
narrow slice beats a broad, flaky one.

the same commit and shout in the team channel — that file is the contract.

Read `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` and `docs/DATA_SETUP.md` first. This doc is
your task list. **Run `npm run ingest` before you do anything else** (see
`docs/DATA_SETUP.md`) — v0 is built around the real datasets, not mock data.

## What already exists (v0, working, grounded in real data)

- Full type model in `src/lib/types.ts` — Vehicle, VehicleComponent,
  Workflow/Stage, Requirement/ScoreFactor, Signal, SourceRecord,
  FeedbackRecord, SalesVolume, CustomerStudyScore, Stakeholder,
  StakeholderReview, AuditLogEntry, AISummary. Read this file top to bottom
  before changing anything; it's the shared vocabulary.
- In-memory store (`src/lib/db.ts`) with full CRUD + an append-only audit
  log. Every mutation function (`createWorkflow`, `updateStage`,
  `updateRequirementStatus`, `updateWeights`, `submitReview`,
  `addAISummary`) already calls `logAction()` — keep this invariant for
  anything new you add: **no mutation without a log entry**.
- **Real ingestion pipeline** (`scripts/ingest-real-data.ts`): parses the 3
  feedback datasets (13,771 real verbatims), sales volumes, and
  multi-market customer studies into `src/data/*.json`. `npm run ingest` to
  run it. See `docs/DATA_SETUP.md` for the full pipeline explanation.
- **Deterministic requirement derivation** (`src/lib/deriveRequirements.ts`):
  turns real signals into scored, evidence-backed `Requirement` objects —
  no LLM involved. This already covers most of what a naive "AI scoring"
  implementation would do, and it's more defensible (every number traces
  to a formula you can point at, not a model's opinion).
- `src/lib/seed.ts` assembles real workflows for all 3 vehicle lines from
  the ingested JSON (`buildRealSeed()`), falling back to a small
  hand-written mock (`buildMockSeed()`) if a teammate hasn't run ingestion
  yet. **Never break the fallback path** — it's what keeps the app
  runnable for anyone without `data-raw/` access yet.
- REST routes for everything in `api-client.ts` — vehicles, components,
  workflows (get/create/by-component), requirements (list/get/patch/
  weights/challenge), signals+sources, audit log, AI summaries,
  stakeholders, reviews, feedback (filtered/paginated, for the Evidence
  Explorer), customer-study comparisons.

## Your tasks, roughly in priority order

### 1. Live ingestion endpoint (US-1.1, 1.3) — upgrade from offline to in-app
Right now ingestion is an offline script (`npm run ingest`), run once by
each teammate against local files. If time allows, build
`POST /api/workflows/:id/ingest` so a PM can upload a new dataset from the
UI and see it flow through without a dev re-running a script. Reuse the
parsing logic already in `scripts/ingest-real-data.ts` — extract the
column-mapping into a shared function both the script and the route can
call. Add the malformed-row flagging the current script skips (AC in
US-1.1): return `{ imported: n, flagged: [...] }` instead of silently
coercing bad rows.

### 2. Web enrichment (US-1.2) — currently missing entirely
There is no external/web `SourceRecord` in the real data pipeline — only
BMW's own 4 datasets. If time allows, add a minimal enrichment step (even
a stubbed/hardcoded set of competitor data points for one or two
components) so every component's evidence isn't 100% internal. Every web
`SourceRecord` needs `url`, `retrievedAt`, and a `reliability` tier
(`review_site`/`forum`/`official`) — the type already supports this, Role
D's Evidence Explorer filter already expects it.

### 3. Multi-market workflows (US-5.1, 5.2)
Each component currently has exactly one active workflow, pinned to one
"primary market" picked in `seed.ts` (`PRIMARY_MARKET`). Real sales data
supports comparing e.g. BMW 5 Series across Europe/China/USA — if time
allows, let a component have one workflow per market and add
`GET /api/components/:id/workflows` returning all of them, so Role C can
build a market switcher on the workflow page.

### 4. Equipment PDF structured parsing (known gap, see `docs/DATA_SETUP.md`)
Currently just text chunks by section. A real per-trim feature matrix
would strengthen competitive/equipment-gap evidence meaningfully — only
attempt this if everything else is solid, it's a brittle parsing problem
(see the doc for specifics on why it was skipped).

### 5. Replace in-memory store with something durable (stretch)
Only if everything else is solid with time to spare. SQLite via
`better-sqlite3` or `drizzle` is the fastest path that still ships before a
hackathon deadline. Keep every exported function signature in `db.ts`
identical; this should be invisible to Roles B/C/D. At 13.7k feedback rows
plus derived data, the in-memory store is already doing real work — this
is a "nice to have for demo-day crash resilience," not an urgent fix.

## Guardrails

- Keep `logAction()` calls accurate: `oldValue`/`newValue` should be real
  values, not placeholders — Role B's AI summaries and the audit trail UI
  both depend on these being meaningful, not decorative.
- **Never commit `data-raw/` or `src/data/*.json`** — both are gitignored
  on purpose, this is confidential BMW hackathon data. Code that reads
  them is fine to commit; the data itself is not. If `git status` ever
  shows either as untracked-but-stageable, something's wrong with
  `.gitignore` — fix the ignore rule, don't `git add -f`.
- Don't let the demo break: the flagship "battery" workflow narrative
  (`buildFlagshipNarrative()` in `seed.ts`) is what gets shown to judges.
  It rebases itself onto whatever the real data computes as the #1 battery
  finding, so re-running ingestion is safe — but don't remove the
  mechanism itself.
- `nanoid` is already a dependency for generating ids — use it instead of
  `Math.random()` or `Date.now()` for anything id-like.

## Files you own

```
src/lib/types.ts
src/lib/db.ts
src/lib/seed.ts
src/lib/realData.ts
src/lib/deriveRequirements.ts
scripts/ingest-real-data.ts
scripts/lib/componentMap.ts
src/app/api/**
```
Coordinate before touching `src/lib/api-client.ts` or `src/lib/ai.ts` —
those are Role B/C/D's primary integration points into your work.

  FeedbackRecord, SalesVolume, CustomerStudyScore, Stakeholder,
  StakeholderReview, AuditLogEntry, AISummary. Read this file top to bottom
  before changing anything; it's the shared vocabulary.
- In-memory store (`src/lib/db.ts`) with full CRUD + an append-only audit
  log. Every mutation function (`createWorkflow`, `updateStage`,
  `updateRequirementStatus`, `updateWeights`, `submitReview`,
  `addAISummary`) already calls `logAction()` — keep this invariant for
  anything new you add: **no mutation without a log entry**.
- **Real ingestion pipeline** (`scripts/ingest-real-data.ts`): parses the 3
  feedback datasets (13,771 real verbatims), sales volumes, and
  multi-market customer studies into `src/data/*.json`. `npm run ingest` to

# Role B — AI / Intelligence

You own `src/lib/ai.ts`. Read `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` and
`docs/DATA_SETUP.md` first, then run `npm run ingest` (see that doc) so
you're testing against real data, not the mock fallback.

**Important framing shift from a typical "AI hackathon app":** scoring and
signal extraction are already real and deterministic —
`src/lib/deriveRequirements.ts` computes `customer_impact`, `frequency`,
`sales_relevance`, `evidence_strength` straight from the ingested BMW
data, with zero LLM calls, and `scripts/lib/componentMap.ts` uses BMW's own
226-category VFC taxonomy instead of asking a model to cluster verbatims
from scratch. **Don't reimplement either of these with an LLM** — a
formula a judge can audit beats a model's opinion, and re-deriving what's
already deterministic just burns budget for a worse result. Your job is
everything *on top of* that real foundation: narrative generation,
re-assessment under challenge, and the two score factors that are
genuinely judgment calls (`competitive_gap`, `strategic_fit`).

## Budget: OpenAI, $70/person

Use the OpenAI SDK (`npm install openai`) with structured outputs
(`response_format: { type: "json_schema" }`, or `zodResponseFormat` from
`openai/helpers/zod`) for anything whose result gets parsed into a typed
object — never regex a free-text response. Keep `OPENAI_API_KEY` in
`.env.local` (template at `.env.local.example`) and only call the SDK
server-side (API routes or this file), never from a client component.

Because scoring/clustering are already deterministic, real LLM calls here
are per-signal or per-requirement — tens to low hundreds of calls for the
whole demo, not per-verbatim (thousands). Budget is not the constraint:
- **gpt-4.1-mini**: fine for `summarizeStakeholderReviews()` and the
  mechanical parts of `extractSignals()`/`deriveRequirement()` if you
  extend those beyond the deterministic pipeline.
- **gpt-4.1**: use for `summarizeDecisionTrail()` and `reassessChallenge()`
  — these are the two functions a judge will see triggered live in a demo
  (the PM-challenge loop), worth the better model.

## How v0 fakes what you're about to make real

`src/lib/seed.ts`'s `buildFlagshipNarrative()` hand-writes one believable
story on the BMW 5 Series / Battery & Charging workflow: an AI-drafted
requirement that restated a complaint instead of being actionable, a PM
challenge, an AI revision citing the real frequency/concentration numbers,
stakeholder reviews, and three `AISummary` entries (`decision_trail`,
`stakeholder_overview`, `limitations`) with pre-written narrative text —
but every number it references (verbatim count, sentiment concentration,
requirement title) is computed live from real data, so re-running
`npm run ingest` doesn't break the story. Your job is to make the *mocked
functions in `ai.ts`* produce that same quality of narrative, generated
for real from the live data instead of templated.

## Your tasks, in priority order

### 1. `summarizeDecisionTrail()` — the most demo-critical function
Input: a `Requirement` + its related `AuditLogEntry[]`. Real
implementation: pass the ordered log entries (especially
`requirement_challenged` entries and the AI's own prior summaries) to
OpenAI and ask for a narrative of what was asked, what was proposed, what
changed and why. Test it by calling `POST /api/requirements/:id` with
`status: "challenged"` and a rationale, then regenerating the summary and
confirming it reflects the new log entry. **This answers "what happens
when a PM disagrees" live, in front of judges** — prioritize it over
everything else in this doc.

### 2. `reassessChallenge()` (US-6.3)
Already wired to `POST /api/requirements/:id/challenge`
(`src/app/api/requirements/[id]/challenge/route.ts`). Must return
`{ changed: boolean, explanation: string }` — US-6.3's acceptance
criterion explicitly requires stating whether the challenge changed the
result, and why. Prompt the model with the requirement's current
`scoreFactors`/`evidenceLevel` and the PM's free-text argument; have it
either adjust `scoreFactors`/`evidenceLevel` (coordinate a new
`updateEvidenceLevel`-style setter with Role A if so) or explain why
nothing changes.

### 3. `summarizeStakeholderReviews()` — the "PR reviewer" AI overview
Input: all `StakeholderReview[]` for a requirement. Real implementation:
synthesize where reviewers agree/disagree and *why*, distinguishing a
process objection (like Legal's in the seeded narrative) from a product
objection. Renders directly in the PM workflow page's stakeholder panel.

### 4. `competitive_gap` and `strategic_fit` — the two genuinely-judgment score factors
Look at `competitiveGap()` and `strategicFit()` in
`src/lib/deriveRequirements.ts`. Both are currently crude defaults (a
customer-study cross-model comparison for gap, a flat
battery/steering-get-70-else-50 heuristic for fit) — these are the
legitimate upgrade targets for an LLM call, specifically because they
require judgment a formula can't give you (is this strategically
important? how big is the gap vs. a real external competitor, not just a
sibling BMW model?). If you do this, keep the same contract: return
`{ value: 0-100, rationale: string, citedSourceIds?: string[] }` and log
the rationale to the audit trail — a bare number with no trace is exactly
what the brief warns against ("make clear where conclusions are based on
evidence vs. assumptions").

### 5. `extractSignals()` and `deriveRequirement()` — only if you want to go beyond the deterministic pipeline
These exist in `ai.ts` as mocks but **the real pipeline doesn't use them**
— `deriveRequirements.ts` does the real work without an LLM. Only touch
these if you want to add an LLM-authored *description* on top of the
template-generated ones in `descriptionFor()` (`deriveRequirements.ts`) —
e.g. a more polished requirement write-up that still cites the same real
verbatims. Don't let this become re-deriving what's already real.

### 6. Contradiction flagging (US-2.7) — currently unpopulated
`Signal.contradicts: string[]` exists in the type and in every ingested
signal, but `scripts/ingest-real-data.ts` never populates it. When two
signals for the same component have opposing sentiment on a related theme
(e.g. a "too many screens" pain point alongside a "love the display" like),
flag it — either a keyword-similarity pass in the ingestion script
(deterministic, cheap) or an LLM pass if the themes aren't textually
similar enough for keywords to catch. Coordinate with Role A since this
touches `scripts/ingest-real-data.ts`, which they own.

## Guardrails

- Every mocked function's docstring in `ai.ts` says exactly what real
  behavior is expected and what shape to return — change bodies, not
  signatures, unless you coordinate with whoever's consuming them.
- Never let an AI call block the UI with no feedback. For judge-facing
  demo reliability, consider pre-generating and caching the flagship
  workflow's `AISummary` entries (call once, store via `addAISummary()`)
  rather than regenerating them live on every page load — the seeded
  narrative is already your fallback if a live call fails mid-demo.

## Files you own

```
src/lib/ai.ts
```
You'll also touch `src/app/api/requirements/[id]/challenge/route.ts`,
`src/lib/deriveRequirements.ts`'s `competitiveGap()`/`strategicFit()`
(coordinate with Role A, who owns that file), and possibly
`scripts/ingest-real-data.ts` for contradiction flagging (also Role A's
file — coordinate).

for real from the live data instead of templated.

three `AISummary` entries (`decision_trail`, `stakeholder_overview`,
`limitations`) with pre-written narrative text. This is what lets the whole
app demo convincingly before any real AI is wired in. Your job is to make
the mocked functions in `ai.ts` produce *that same quality of narrative*,
generated from real data instead of hand-written.

## Setup

Use the Anthropic SDK with model `claude-sonnet-5`. Get an API key from
whoever on the team has one; store it in `.env.local` as
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (already gitignored). Keep all AI calls server-side
(inside API routes or `lib/ai.ts`, never from a client component) so the
key never ships to the browser.

```bash
npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk
```

## Your tasks, in priority order

### 1. `summarizeDecisionTrail()` (US-9.3, and the "AI summary updates
when PM asks for changes" mechanic from the brief)
Input: a `Requirement` + its related `AuditLogEntry[]` (already wired —
see how `GET /api/workflows/:id/ai-summaries` and the seed seed this).

`requirement_challenged` and the AI's own prior summaries) to Claude and
ask for a narrative of what was asked, what was proposed, what changed and
why. **This is the single most demo-critical function** — it's the thing
that answers "what happens when a PM disagrees" live, in front of judges.

and a rationale, then regenerating the summary and confirming it reflects

(`src/app/api/requirements/[id]/challenge/route.ts`). Must return
`{ changed: boolean, explanation: string }` — the AC in US-6.3 explicitly
requires stating whether the challenge changed the result, and why. Prompt
Claude with the requirement's current scoreFactors/evidence and the PM's
free-text argument; have it either adjust `scoreFactors`/`evidenceLevel`
(if so, also call `updateWeights` or extend `db.ts` with a
`updateEvidenceLevel` setter — coordinate with Role A) or explain why
nothing changes.

### 3. `summarizeStakeholderReviews()` (the "PR reviewer" AI overview)
Input: all `StakeholderReview[]` for a requirement. Real implementation:
synthesize where reviewers agree/disagree and *why*, distinguishing a
process objection (like Legal's in the seed data) from a product objection.
This renders directly in the PM workflow page's stakeholder panel.

### 4. `extractSignals()` and `deriveRequirement()` (Epics 2 and 3)
Only once ingestion (Role A) produces real `SourceRecord[]` from uploaded
verbatims. `extractSignals` clusters verbatims into themes with frequency/
sentiment (US-2.1); `deriveRequirement` turns one signal + its sources into
a draft requirement with evidence level, assumptions, uncertainties
(US-3.1). Evidence level should be a real function of source count/
reliability, not vibes — e.g. strong = 3+ sources including first-party,
moderate = 2, weak = 1 or web-only. Keep regulatory/engineering/pricing

props.

  than the SVG placeholder, lowest risk.
- A real 360 spin (frame sequence + drag-to-rotate, or an embed) if time
  allows — keep the hotspot *positions* driven by data
  (`VehicleComponent.hotspot`), not hardcoded per-frame, or hotspots will
  drift when the car rotates. If you go this route, hotspots probably only
  need to render on the default/front-3-4 frame for v0; don't over-build.
Either way: the "blue dot = has workflow, gray dot = create new" affordance
already works (`CarHotspotViewer` colors by `component.workflowId`) — keep
it.

### 2. Pipeline strip polish (US-9.1)
`PipelineStrip.tsx` already shows stage status (pending/active/complete/
blocked) with hover tooltips (owner, timestamps). As Role A wires real
`ingest`/`enrich` stage transitions, confirm the strip updates live
(poll or re-fetch on an interval, or add a manual refresh button — v0 has
neither, pick whichever is faster to ship). Consider a "re-run pipeline"
button once Role A's US-9.2 lands.

### 3. Sensitivity view (US-4.4, stretch)
`RequirementCard` already lets the PM drag weight sliders and see the score
recompute live (`computeLiveScore`) before saving. For US-4.4, add a view
showing which requirements change rank most as weights shift — this is
naturally a small chart (e.g. a rank-change table or sparkline per
requirement) on the workflow page. Don't build a generic charting library
integration for this — a handful of divs with computed widths (see the bar
"chart" pattern already used in the stakeholder page) is enough.

### 4. Multi-requirement stakeholder panel
Right now the stakeholder review panel on the workflow page scopes to one
`selectedReq` at a time (click a requirement card to select it). If you
have time, consider a workflow-level view that shows review status across
*all* requirements at a glance (e.g. a small reviewer-x-requirement grid),
similar to a PR's "required reviewers" list — only worth it if Role A has
wired multiple requirements with multiple reviews by then.

### 5. Market/vehicle switcher (US-5.1, depends on Role A)
Once Role A exposes multiple workflows per component (different markets),
add a market selector on the workflow page header.

## Guardrails

- Every write action (approve/reject/postpone/challenge/weights) already
  calls `onRequirementChanged` → triggers a full `refresh()` of audit log +
  summaries. Don't bypass this — the audit trail updating live after every
  PM action is core to the demo narrative, not a nice-to-have.
- Reject/postpone require a rationale — this is enforced client-side in
  `RequirementCard` *and* server-side in the API route. Don't remove either
  check.
- Keep the dark theme (`bmw` color tokens in `tailwind.config.ts`) — it's
  already wired through every component.

## Files you own

```
src/app/page.tsx
src/app/workflow/[componentId]/page.tsx
src/components/CarHotspotViewer.tsx
src/components/PipelineStrip.tsx
src/components/RequirementCard.tsx
```
`AuditLogPanel.tsx`, `EvidenceBadge.tsx`, and `ReviewerRow.tsx` are shared
with Role D — coordinate before changing their props.

# Role D — Frontend: Stakeholder & Trust Experience

You own the stakeholder review page, the Evidence Explorer, and the audit
trail — everything about making the app's reasoning *inspectable*. Read
`docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` and `docs/DATA_SETUP.md` first, run
`npm run ingest` (see that doc), then `npm run dev` and click through
`/stakeholder/wf_g60_battery/sh_design` and `/evidence` before changing
anything — both already run end to end against the real 13,771-row
dataset.

## What already exists (v0, working, real data)

- `src/app/stakeholder/[workflowId]/[stakeholderId]/page.tsx` — the
  stakeholder's view: a "summary so far" AI panel, a real customer-study
  comparison chart (`GroupedBarChart`) when the workflow's component maps
  to a benchmarked category, a read-only requirement list with evidence
  badges and real per-factor score bars (`MetricBar`), and a review form
  per requirement assigned to this stakeholder. Submitting disables the
  form and timestamps it, round-trips to `PATCH /api/reviews/:id` →
  `submitReview()` in `db.ts` → audit log entry → the PM's workflow page
  picks it up on next refresh.
- **`src/app/evidence/page.tsx` — the Evidence Explorer, already built**:
  a filterable, paginated table over all 13,771 real feedback rows
  (vehicle, component, feedback type, country, free-text search), backed
  by `GET /api/feedback` and `GET /api/feedback/facets`
  (`src/app/api/feedback/**`). This is your base to extend, not a
  from-scratch task — see tasks below.
- `src/components/charts/MetricBar.tsx` and `GroupedBarChart.tsx` — real
  SVG charts (gridlines, axis labels, no div-width-as-bar-chart), used on
  the stakeholder page and ready to reuse anywhere else you need one.
- `src/components/EvidenceBadge.tsx` — strong/moderate/weak pill, shared
  with Role C.
- `src/components/AuditLogPanel.tsx` — the append-only log list, already
  has an actor-type filter (all/ai/pm/stakeholder) built in. Currently
  lives embedded in the PM workflow page's sidebar only.
- No login/auth — `stakeholderId` is just a route param. Intentional for
  v0, don't build auth.

## Your tasks, in priority order

### 1. Audit log CSV/JSON export (US-8.4)
No export button exists yet. Add one to wherever `AuditLogPanel` renders,
pulling from `GET /api/workflows/:id/audit-log`. Client-side generation
(`entries.map(...).join(',')` + `Blob` + `<a download>`) is the whole
feature, no backend change needed.

### 2. Standalone/dedicated audit trail view (US-8.1)
`AuditLogPanel` only appears embedded in the PM workflow page's sidebar
today. A dedicated route or drawer with more room — plus a "jump to full
evidence chain" affordance (requirement → scoring → signals → source
records, US-8.1) — would strengthen traceability. The evidence accordion
already on the workflow page (grouped by signal, sorted by frequency) is
the thing to deep-link into.

### 3. Low-confidence / needs-decision queue (US-7.2)
A view surfacing requirements where `evidenceLevel === "weak"` or
`status === "challenged"` across *all* workflows, not just the one you're
currently looking at — right now a PM has to visit each workflow to find
these. Could be a new route (`/needs-review`) querying across workflows,
or a counter badge on the landing page per vehicle. Coordinate with Role C
if it touches the landing page.

### 4. Evidence Explorer: drill-down from a signal
The workflow page's evidence accordion shows up to 8 sample sources per
signal; the Evidence Explorer shows all matching rows. Wire a link from an
accordion entry straight into `/evidence?vehicleCode=...&component=...`
with the theme pre-filled into the search box — currently the link only
pre-filters by vehicle+component, not by theme/category.

### 5. Source reliability filter refinement (US-1.3)
`FeedbackRecord`/`SourceRecord` already carry `reliability` for web
sources once Role A's enrichment step (`docs/ROLE_A_BACKEND.md` task 2)
lands real external data — today everything in the real pipeline is
`first_party` (internal verbatims), so a reliability filter on the
Evidence Explorer has nothing to differentiate yet. Revisit once Role A's
web sources exist.

## Guardrails

- Stakeholder review submission is one-shot by design (disabled after
  submit) — don't add an edit-after-submit flow without coordinating with
  Role A, since it changes audit log semantics.
- AI-sourced content uses a left-accent-bar convention (sky=summary,
  violet=overview, amber=limitations/uncertainty) — reuse it, don't invent
  a new visual language for AI content.
- The Evidence Explorer currently reads `src/data/feedback.json` fresh on
  every request (`loadFeedback()` in `src/lib/realData.ts`) — fine at 14k
  rows for a hackathon demo. If you add more filters, filter client-side
  against an already-fetched page rather than adding more round-trips per
  keystroke.

## Files you own

```
src/app/stakeholder/[workflowId]/[stakeholderId]/page.tsx
src/app/evidence/page.tsx
src/app/api/feedback/**
src/components/AuditLogPanel.tsx
src/components/ReviewerRow.tsx
src/components/charts/*.tsx
```
`EvidenceBadge.tsx` is shared with Role C — coordinate before changing its
props.

  sidebar.
- Note there's currently no login/auth — `stakeholderId` is just a route
  param. That's intentional for v0; don't build auth, it's out of scope for
  the hackathon.

## Your tasks, in priority order

### 1. Standalone audit trail / traceability view (US-8.1, 8.4)
Right now `AuditLogPanel` only appears embedded in the PM workflow page.
Build a dedicated, filterable view — either a route like
`/workflow/[componentId]/audit` or a modal/drawer triggered from the
workflow page. Must support (US-8.4): filter by requirement, actor type,
action type, and date range. Each entry already has everything needed
(`AuditLogEntry` in `types.ts`) — this is a filtering/UI task, not a data
task. A "jump to full evidence chain" affordance (US-8.1: requirement →
scoring → consolidation → signals → source records) is the stretch version
— clicking a requirement in the log could open the evidence accordion
already built into the PM workflow page (`signals.map(...)` section),
scrolled/highlighted to the relevant signal.

### 2. Export the audit log (US-8.4)
A "Download CSV" or "Download JSON" button on your audit trail view, pulling
from `GET /api/workflows/:id/audit-log`. Client-side CSV generation (no
backend change needed) is enough — `entries.map(e => [...]).join(',')`
plus a `Blob`/`<a download>` is the whole feature.

### 3. Limitations panel, promoted and reusable (US-7.3)
The PM workflow page already renders an `AISummary` of type `"limitations"`
inline near the bottom. Consider: does this need its own visible affordance
higher up the page (a persistent banner/badge) rather than being the last
thing a PM scrolls to? You own the call — the goal is "I know the data's
reach" being obvious, not buried. Also surface it on the stakeholder page
if there's a workflow-level limitations summary by the time Role B's real
summaries are wired in.

### 4. Low-confidence queue (US-7.2)
A "needs your decision" view: requirements where `evidenceLevel === "weak"`
or `status === "challenged"`, surfaced prominently rather than mixed into
the main requirement list. Could be a filter/tab on the PM workflow page's
requirement list, or a small counter badge in the header. Coordinate with
Role C since this touches the page they also own — this is a good joint
task if either of you finishes early.

### 5. Source reliability filter (US-1.3, depends on Role A's ingestion)
Once Role A's ingestion assigns `reliability` tiers to real sources, add a
filter control on the evidence/sources accordion (already on the PM
workflow page) to show/hide by `first_party` / `official` / `review_site` /
`forum`.

## Guardrails

- Stakeholder review submission is one-shot by design (disabled after
  submit, per the "PR reviewer" mental model) — don't add an edit-after-
  submit flow unless the team explicitly decides reviewers should be able
  to revise, since that changes the audit log semantics (Role A would need
  to add a new action type).
- Anything you show as "AI-generated" should visually read as such — reuse
  the violet/sky color convention already used for AI-sourced panels
  (`AuditLogPanel`'s `ACTOR_COLOR.ai`, the sky-tinted decision-trail panel)
  rather than inventing a new convention.
- Don't fetch the full audit log on every keystroke if you add filtering —
  fetch once per workflow, filter client-side; the log is small enough
  (tens of entries) for this hackathon's scope.

## Files you own

```
src/app/stakeholder/[workflowId]/[stakeholderId]/page.tsx
src/components/AuditLogPanel.tsx
src/components/ReviewerRow.tsx
```
`EvidenceBadge.tsx` is shared with Role C — coordinate before changing its
props.

# Milestones (15-17h build)

v0 already exists on `main` as of kickoff: landing page, PM workflow page,
stakeholder review page, in-memory store, mocked AI layer, one fully
populated demo workflow (BMW 5 Series / Battery & Charging / Europe), all
wired end to end and verified working. Everyone starts from a running app,
not a blank repo — `npm install && npm run dev` should work immediately.

Times are elapsed-from-kickoff, not wall-clock — shift to fit your actual
start time. Each role's detailed task list is in its own doc
(`ROLE_A_BACKEND.md`, `ROLE_B_AI.md`, `ROLE_C_PM_FRONTEND.md`,
`ROLE_D_STAKEHOLDER_TRUST.md`).

## H0 — Kickoff (30 min)
- Everyone: clone, `npm install`, `npm run dev`, click through all three
  views against the seeded data. Confirm you understand the demo narrative
  in `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` before writing code.
- Agree on branch strategy: short-lived feature branches off `main`, small
  PRs, merge often (every 1-2h) to avoid a brutal integration at H14. A
  stale branch in a 16h hackathon is a dead branch.
- Role A: get an Anthropic API key into the team's hands for Role B.
- Everyone: confirm Node version (`node -v`) — 18.17+ required, 20+ fine.

## H0:30 - H4 — Parallel build, independent tracks
- **Role A**: dataset ingestion endpoint (US-1.1) — CSV/paste upload for the
  four dataset types, malformed-row flagging, `SourceRecord` creation.
  Start on a second seeded component (e.g. "interior") in parallel so
  there's a second demo-able story by H8.
- **Role B**: wire the Anthropic SDK, get `summarizeDecisionTrail()`
  producing real output against the seeded battery audit log. This is the
  highest-leverage function in the app — prioritize it over everything
  else in your doc.
- **Role C**: real car visual for the landing page (static image + hotspot
  overlay, minimum; 360 viewer if time allows). This is the first thing
  judges see — don't let it stay a wireframe SVG past H4.
- **Role D**: standalone audit trail view with filtering (US-8.1, 8.4).

**Checkpoint H4**: everyone demos their piece to the group, 2 min each.
Merge anything stable into `main`.

## H4 - H8 — Integration + depth
- **Role A**: wire real `ingest`/`enrich` stage transitions to the pipeline
  strip so Role C's UI shows real progress, not just seeded "complete"
  states. Start on multi-market support if ingestion is solid.
- **Role B**: `reassessChallenge()` and `summarizeStakeholderReviews()` real
  implementations. Test the full "PM challenges → AI re-assesses → states
  whether it changed" loop live against the UI.
- **Role C**: pipeline strip polish, live-refresh on stage changes, start
  the sensitivity view (US-4.4) if the weight-slider mechanic needs it to
  feel complete.
- **Role D**: audit log CSV export, low-confidence queue (US-7.2).

**Checkpoint H8 (roughly halfway)**: full run-through as a group, PM
persona end to end: land → open/create a workflow → review requirements →
challenge one → see stakeholder reviews come in → approve. Fix anything
that breaks this path before adding more features — this path *is* the
demo.

## H8 - H12 — Breadth + second component
- Get a second component (beyond battery) demo-ready end to end, ideally
  one where the PM *rejects* a requirement (shows the full decision
  spectrum, not just approve). Role A seeds/ingests it, Role B's AI
  functions run against it for real, Roles C/D confirm the UI holds up
  with different data shapes (e.g. a requirement with zero stakeholder
  reviews yet, or all-reject).
- Epic 2 signal extraction (`extractSignals`, Role B) from real verbatims,
  if ingestion (Role A) is ready.
- Stretch items from each role's doc, time permitting, in the priority
  order listed there — don't start a role's "stretch" section if their
  "must have" isn't demo-stable yet.

## H12 - H14 — Feature freeze, bug bash
- **No new features after H12** unless something is badly broken. Switch
  entirely to: click through every view on a clean `npm install && npm run
  dev`, fix what's broken, tighten copy, fix loading/empty states.
- Confirm `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx next lint` are both clean.
- Confirm the demo narrative survives a hard refresh at every step (no
  state that only exists because of a specific click order).

## H14 - H16 — Demo prep
- Write the 3-minute demo script: landing page (show the concept) → open
  battery workflow (show pipeline + AI summary) → challenge a requirement
  live (show the AI re-assessment loop — this is your best "wow" moment) →
  switch to stakeholder view, submit a review (show it land back in the PM
  view's audit trail) → show the audit log / traceability view (prove the
  "transparent decision-support" claim from the brief).
- Record a fallback screen capture of the full demo in case live demo
  breaks — `npm run build && npm run start` once to confirm production
  build works, not just dev mode.
- Prepare the pitch framing around the evaluation criteria table in
  `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` — name-check "decision and scoring logic",
  "traceability and auditability", etc. explicitly, since that's literally
  how this gets scored.

## H16 - H17 — Buffer
Things go wrong. This hour exists so that when they do, you're not cutting
into demo prep.

# Milestones (15-17h build)

v0 already exists on `main` as of kickoff — and it's further along than a
typical hackathon starting point: landing page with a vehicle switcher
across all 3 BMW lines, PM workflow page, stakeholder review page, an
Evidence Explorer over real data, in-memory store, mocked AI layer (OpenAI
target), and **real BMW data already flowing through a deterministic
derivation+scoring pipeline** — 13,771 real verbatims, real sales volumes,
real customer-study benchmarks, ~17 real component workflows across 3
vehicle lines, one fully narrated flagship workflow (BMW 5 Series /
Battery & Charging). All wired end to end and verified working. Everyone
starts from a running, data-grounded app, not a blank repo or a mock demo.

Times are elapsed-from-kickoff, not wall-clock — shift to fit your actual
start time. Each role's detailed task list is in its own doc
(`ROLE_A_BACKEND.md`, `ROLE_B_AI.md`, `ROLE_C_PM_FRONTEND.md`,
`ROLE_D_STAKEHOLDER_TRUST.md`).

## H0 — Kickoff (30 min)
- Everyone: clone, `npm install`. Get the real dataset files (see
  `docs/DATA_SETUP.md`) into `data-raw/`, run `npm run ingest`, then
  `npm run dev` and click through all views against the real data. Confirm
  you understand the demo narrative in `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` before
  writing code.
- Agree on branch strategy: short-lived feature branches off `main`, small
  PRs, merge often (every 1-2h) to avoid a brutal integration at H14. A
  stale branch in a 16h hackathon is a dead branch.
- Role A: get an OpenAI API key into the team's hands for Role B (budget:
  $70/person — see `docs/ROLE_B_AI.md` for why that's plenty).
- Everyone: confirm Node version (`node -v`) — 18.17+ required, 20+ fine.
- **Reminder**: `data-raw/` and `src/data/*.json` are gitignored on
  purpose — confidential hackathon data, never `git add -f` them.

## H0:30 - H4 — Parallel build, independent tracks
- **Role A**: dataset ingestion endpoint (US-1.1) — CSV/paste upload for the
  four dataset types, malformed-row flagging, `SourceRecord` creation.
  Start on a second seeded component (e.g. "interior") in parallel so
  there's a second demo-able story by H8.
- **Role B**: wire the Anthropic SDK, get `summarizeDecisionTrail()`
  producing real output against the seeded battery audit log. This is the
  highest-leverage function in the app — prioritize it over everything
  else in your doc.
- **Role C**: real car visual for the landing page (static image + hotspot
  overlay, minimum; 360 viewer if time allows). This is the first thing
  judges see — don't let it stay a wireframe SVG past H4.
- **Role D**: standalone audit trail view with filtering (US-8.1, 8.4).

**Checkpoint H4**: everyone demos their piece to the group, 2 min each.
Merge anything stable into `main`.

## H4 - H8 — Integration + depth
- **Role A**: wire real `ingest`/`enrich` stage transitions to the pipeline
  strip so Role C's UI shows real progress, not just seeded "complete"
  states. Start on multi-market support if ingestion is solid.
- **Role B**: `reassessChallenge()` and `summarizeStakeholderReviews()` real
  implementations. Test the full "PM challenges → AI re-assesses → states
  whether it changed" loop live against the UI.
- **Role C**: pipeline strip polish, live-refresh on stage changes, start
  the sensitivity view (US-4.4) if the weight-slider mechanic needs it to
  feel complete.
- **Role D**: audit log CSV export, low-confidence queue (US-7.2).

**Checkpoint H8 (roughly halfway)**: full run-through as a group, PM
persona end to end: land → open/create a workflow → review requirements →
challenge one → see stakeholder reviews come in → approve. Fix anything
that breaks this path before adding more features — this path *is* the
demo.

## H8 - H12 — Breadth + second component
- Get a second component (beyond battery) demo-ready end to end, ideally
  one where the PM *rejects* a requirement (shows the full decision
  spectrum, not just approve). Role A seeds/ingests it, Role B's AI
  functions run against it for real, Roles C/D confirm the UI holds up
  with different data shapes (e.g. a requirement with zero stakeholder
  reviews yet, or all-reject).
- Epic 2 signal extraction (`extractSignals`, Role B) from real verbatims,
  if ingestion (Role A) is ready.
- Stretch items from each role's doc, time permitting, in the priority
  order listed there — don't start a role's "stretch" section if their
  "must have" isn't demo-stable yet.

## H12 - H14 — Feature freeze, bug bash
- **No new features after H12** unless something is badly broken. Switch
  entirely to: click through every view on a clean `npm install && npm run
  dev`, fix what's broken, tighten copy, fix loading/empty states.
- Confirm `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx next lint` are both clean.
- Confirm the demo narrative survives a hard refresh at every step (no
  state that only exists because of a specific click order).

## H14 - H16 — Demo prep
- Write the 3-minute demo script: landing page (show the concept) → open
  battery workflow (show pipeline + AI summary) → challenge a requirement
  live (show the AI re-assessment loop — this is your best "wow" moment) →
  switch to stakeholder view, submit a review (show it land back in the PM
  view's audit trail) → show the audit log / traceability view (prove the
  "transparent decision-support" claim from the brief).
- Record a fallback screen capture of the full demo in case live demo
  breaks — `npm run build && npm run start` once to confirm production
  build works, not just dev mode.
- Prepare the pitch framing around the evaluation criteria table in
  `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` — name-check "decision and scoring logic",
  "traceability and auditability", etc. explicitly, since that's literally
  how this gets scored.

## H16 - H17 — Buffer
Things go wrong. This hour exists so that when they do, you're not cutting
into demo prep.

Confirmed — only `.gitkeep` would ever be staged from `src/data/`; the real JSON fixtures stay local-only. Everything's verified clean. Here's the summary of what changed:

## Redesigned around real data

I pulled apart your 8 real BMW files (13,771 feedback rows across F70/G60/G70, sales volumes, multi-market customer studies, option-list PDFs) and built an actual ingestion pipeline instead of hand-written fixtures:

- **`scripts/ingest-real-data.ts`** + **`scripts/lib/componentMap.ts`** — parses the real datasets, and maps BMW's own 226-category VFC feedback taxonomy onto our 6 landing-page components (keyword-based, auditable, not an LLM guess)
- **`src/lib/deriveRequirements.ts`** — deterministic requirement scoring from real frequency/sentiment/sales-growth/customer-study-gap data, zero LLM calls needed for this part
- **`src/lib/seed.ts`** now builds ~17 real component workflows across all 3 vehicle lines, with one flagship narrative (5 Series battery) rebased onto whatever the real data computes as the top finding
- **New Evidence Explorer** (`/evidence`) — filterable, paginated table over all 13,771 real rows
- Real customer-study comparison charts and score-factor bars (SVG, no library)

**Privacy**: `data-raw/` and `src/data/*.json` are gitignored — confidential BMW data never touches the public repo. Code is tracked, data isn't. Each teammate needs their own copy (`docs/DATA_SETUP.md` has the 2-minute setup).

## UI: "heavily functional, not AI slop"

Swapped rounded-xl gradient panels for bordered, dense, monospace-numbers enterprise-tool styling across every component — left-accent-bars instead of tinted bubbles for AI content, real data tables, real charts. Also fixed a CSS Grid overflow bug along the way (`body`'s stray `flex` was letting wide descendants stretch the whole page).

## OpenAI, not Anthropic

Repointed `ai.ts` and all docs to target OpenAI per your $70/person budget — with a concrete note that the deterministic scoring already means LLM calls are per-signal/requirement (tens, not thousands), so budget isn't actually the constraint.

All docs (`README`, `PROJECT_BRIEF`, all 4 role docs, new `DATA_SETUP.md`) are updated to match. Build/lint/typecheck all clean. Nothing's committed yet — want me to commit this?

content.content:
# Page Overview

This is **not** a hackathon submission platform. Instead, it's a **developer guide** for teams participating in EHL Munich 2026 who want to build projects using Entire, a git forge platform for AI-native teams.

## What Teams Should Do Regarding GitHub Repos

The page does **not** establish naming conventions, submission requirements, or mandatory files for hackathon participation. Rather, it provides optional technical setup instructions for those choosing to work with Entire.

### Key GitHub Setup Steps

1. **Authorization**: "Everyone on the team signs in to Entire with Sign in with GitHub and authorizes the Entire GitHub App"

2. **Admin Configuration**: A GitHub organization administrator must install the Entire GitHub App and import the repository through their onboarding process. The guide notes that "access follows the GitHub collaborator list."

3. **CLI Installation**: Teams should install the Entire CLI and run `entire enable` in their repository to begin capturing agent sessions.

4. **No Special Naming/Registration**: The page contains no requirements for repository naming conventions, team registration forms, or designated submission repositories. Access is automatic for GitHub collaborators after admin setup.

## Bottom Line

This guide helps teams *optionally enhance* their hackathon projects with Entire's tools for tracking AI agent work—it's not a mandatory hackathon submission framework.

content.content:
# Entire at EHL Munich 2026: Key Setup Information

## Event Details
October 10–11, 2026 in Munich, Germany. The event features Entire, described as "the git forge for AI-native teams."

## Core Concept
Entire captures AI coding agent sessions alongside git commits, preserving reasoning and decisions within repositories. The platform enables "Continuous Memory" through its Graph and Brain features.

## Repository Connection Steps

**Sign-in Phase:**
"Everyone on the team signs in to Entire with Sign in with GitHub and authorizes the Entire GitHub App."

**Admin Import:**
A GitHub organization administrator must install the Entire GitHub App and import the repository. "Access follows the GitHub collaborator list."

## Initial CLI Setup

The installation commands provided are:

**macOS/Linux:**
```
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows:**
```
irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex
```

**Enable in repository:**
```
entire enable
```

## First Checkpoint Workflow

After making agent-driven code changes:

```
git add path/to/changed-file
git commit -m "Build my first feature with Entire"
entire checkpoint list
entire checkpoint explain HEAD
```

## Key Features Mentioned

- **Checkpoints**: Connect commits to agent sessions
- **Agentic Search**: Semantic search across sessions
- **Entire Graph**: "Can save up to 71% in token spend"
- **Entire Brain**: Persistent memory layer across agents
- **Trails**: Code review reimagined for AI workflows

## Support Channels

- Discord: #entire channel during EHL Munich
- Contact: Haimantika (@haimantika) and Joseph (@jkcso)
- Community: [discord.gg/XzhmCqcmQ](https://discord.gg/XzhmCqcmQ)

No problem — here's where things stand and what's left.

## Done
- Repo created and pushed: **[NavneetKishanS/ehl-alpha](https://github.com/NavneetKishanS/ehl-alpha)** (public)

## Left for you (manual — these are account sign-ins and a third-party installer, not something I should do on your behalf)

**1. Add teammates as collaborators** (whenever you have their usernames):
```bash
gh repo add-collaborator NavneetKishanS/ehl-alpha <username> --permission push
```
Or via the UI: https://github.com/NavneetKishanS/ehl-alpha/settings/access

**2. Each teammate signs in to Entire** at hack.entire.io with "Sign in with GitHub" and authorizes the Entire GitHub App.

**3. You (as the repo owner) install the Entire GitHub App and import the repo** — this is the "org admin" step in the guide; since the repo is under your personal account, you're the one who does this. Entire's access then follows the collaborator list from step 1.

**4. Install the Entire CLI** (run this yourself — I don't execute third-party installer scripts even official-looking ones):
```bash
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
```

**5. Enable it in the repo and make a first checkpoint:**
```bash
cd /Users/navneetkishansrinivasan/Desktop/ehl-alpha
entire enable
git add <changed files>
git commit -m "Build my first feature with Entire"
entire checkpoint list
entire checkpoint explain HEAD
```

Once you've run `entire enable` yourself, I'm happy to keep working in this repo as normal — `entire` just observes commits alongside our sessions, it shouldn't change anything about how we work together.

taxonomy maps feedback onto our 6 components, and requirement scoring is
computed deterministically from real frequency/sentiment/sales/customer-

factors) in place of div-width bars.

Redesigns every component to a denser, bordered, monospace-numbers style
in place of the rounded-xl gradient-panel look, and repoints the AI layer
(still mocked) at OpenAI per the team's budget instead of Anthropic.

Real data (data-raw/, src/data/*.json) stays gitignored throughout; only
the pipeline code that reads it is committed.

EOF
)"
